QF.id: Taxation of Debt and Equity Products_C2_5

question.text: Scenario: Suresh Iyer, aged 55, is a resident Indian with total taxable income of Rs. 16,00,000 (in the 20% slab under new regime FY 2025-26, effective marginal rate approximately 20% plus cess). He is evaluating five investment options for a lump sum of Rs. 10,00,000 with a 2-year horizon: Option 1: Bank Fixed Deposit at 7.5% p.a. (compounded annually). Interest taxable at slab rate. Option 2: Listed Corporate Bond (NCD) yielding 8% p.a. coupon (paid annually). If held >12 months and sold, LTCG at 12.5%. Option 3: Equity Mutual Fund with expected NAV growth of 12% p.a. (no dividend). If held >12 months, LTCG at 12.5% above Rs. 1.25 lakh under s.112A. Option 4: Gold Mutual Fund with expected NAV growth of 10% p.a. Holding >24 months = LTCG at 12.5% without indexation. Option 5: Debt Mutual Fund (85% in debt, purchased after 1-Apr-2023) with expected NAV growth of 7.5% p.a. Always taxed as STCG at slab rate under s.50AA. Assume: New tax regime with no deductions. Suresh's marginal tax rate for additional income is 20% (in the Rs. 16-20 lakh slab). Ignore surcharge. Health & Education cess is 4%. Effective marginal rate = 20% x 1.04 = 20.8%. For s.112A, assume no other LTCG, so Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption is available. Question 5 of 5: Comparing all five options, which gives the highest post-tax CAGR, and which option carries the highest "tax drag" (difference between pre-tax and post-tax CAGR)?

answer.text: Equity MF has the highest post-tax CAGR (~11.2%); among the listed options the highest tax drag is on the NCD (~1.85%)
Gold MF has the highest post-tax CAGR (~8.8%); tax drag is uniform across all options at approximately 1.5%
NCD has the highest post-tax CAGR (~6.15%); tax drag is lowest for NCD and highest for Equity MF
All five options have similar post-tax CAGRs between 6-7% because higher pre-tax returns attract proportionally higher taxes

explanation.text: The Logic: Comprehensive comparison of all five options: Option 1 - Bank FD: Pre-tax CAGR = 7.50%. Post-tax CAGR approx 5.98%. Tax drag = 7.50% - 5.98% = 1.52%. Option 2 - Listed NCD: Pre-tax CAGR = 8.00% (coupon taxed at slab; redemption at par). Post-tax CAGR approx 6.15%. Tax drag = 8.00% - 6.15% = 1.85%. Option 3 - Equity MF: Pre-tax CAGR = 12.00%. After applying s.112A (12.5% LTCG above the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption), post-tax CAGR is approx 11.2%. Tax drag = 12.00% - 11.2% = 0.80%. Option 4 - Gold MF: Pre-tax CAGR = 10.00%. Post-tax CAGR approx 8.8%. Tax drag = 10.00% - 8.8% = 1.20%. Option 5 - Debt MF (post-Apr 2023, s.50AA): Pre-tax CAGR = 7.50%. Post-tax CAGR approx 5.98%. Tax drag = 7.50% - 5.98% = 1.52%. Rankings by post-tax CAGR: Equity MF (11.2%) > Gold MF (8.8%) > NCD (6.15%) > FD = Debt MF (5.98%). Rankings by tax drag (highest = least tax-efficient): NCD (1.85%) > FD = Debt MF (1.52%) > Gold MF (1.20%) > Equity MF (0.80%). Equity MF has both the highest post-tax CAGR and the lowest tax drag, thanks to the lower 12.5% LTCG rate under s.112A and the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption. The NCD carries the highest tax drag because its full coupon is taxed at slab rate every year. The Trap: Option B wrongly claims tax drag is uniform - the whole point of differential product taxation is that drag varies. Option C wrongly ranks NCD highest on post-tax CAGR. Option D wrongly assumes proportional taxation across asset classes. Note: Source - NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser (Level 2) workbook, pages on SWP/debt MF slab taxation, specified mutual funds, equity MF taxation, the summary tax table, and Gold ETFs (pp. 110, 215-217, 239-245, 255-256, 287-288).
